definitions.definition: u_t(x,t)=∂u(x,t)/∂t, component by component. Derivatives are the usual real derivatives; a derivative not existing is assigned the total derivative convention value zero. When u is smooth on its open domain these are classical derivatives.
u_tt(x,t)=∂u_t(x,t)/∂t, component by component, with the same total derivative convention.

definitions.type: family indexed by j∈{1,…,n} of maps ℝ^n × (0,∞) → ℝ^m
definitions.definition: u_j(j,x,t)=∂_{x_j}u(x,t), the derivative along the jth standard coordinate direction, component by component with the total derivative convention. We also write u_j when the index j is explicitly fixed.

definitions.type: family indexed by j∈{1,…,n} of maps ℝ^n × (0,∞) → ℝ^m
definitions.definition: u_jj(j,x,t)=∂_{x_j}u_j(j,x,t), with the total derivative convention. The notation u_jj with fixed j has this same meaning.
Δu(x,t)=∑_{j=1}^n u_jj(j,x,t), the componentwise spatial Laplacian Δ_xu of the input.

inputs.statement: u is jointly smooth on the open set ℝ^n × (0,∞).
For every x∈ℝ^n and every t>0, |u(x,t)|=1.
For every x∈ℝ^n and every t>0 there exists a real scalar a such that u_tt(x,t)−Δu(x,t)=a u(x,t). No regularity of such scalars as a function of (x,t) is assumed.

inputs.statement: Let K be an RCLike field, W an inner product space over K (and normed additive commutative group) also carrying a real normed-space structure, and f,g:ℝ→W. If f and g are real differentiable at a real point z, then deriv(t↦⟨f(t),g(t)⟩_K)(z)=⟨f(z),deriv g(z)⟩_K+⟨deriv f(z),g(z)⟩_K.

binders.type: normed additive commutative group, inner product space over K, and real normed space

hypotheses: K is RCLike; W has the stated normed group, K-inner-product and real normed-space structures.
f is real differentiable at z.
g is real differentiable at z.
source_contract.signature:
@deriv_inner_apply : ∀ (𝕜 : Type u_1) {E : Type u_2} [inst : RCLike.{u_1} 𝕜] [inst_1 : NormedAddCommGroup.{u_2} E]
  [inst_2 : InnerProductSpace.{u_1, u_2} 𝕜 E] [inst_3 : NormedSpace.{0, u_2} ℝ E] {f g : ℝ → E} {x : ℝ},
  DifferentiableAt.{0, 0, u_2} ℝ f x →
    DifferentiableAt.{0, 0, u_2} ℝ g x →
      Eq.{u_1 + 1} (deriv.{0, u_1} (fun t => inner.{u_1, u_2} 𝕜 (f t) (g t)) x)
        (HAdd.hAdd.{u_1, u_1, u_1} (inner.{u_1, u_2} 𝕜 (f x) (deriv.{0, u_2} g x))
          (inner.{u_1, u_2} 𝕜 (deriv.{0, u_2} f x) (g x)))

output.statement: For every x∈ℝ^n and t>0, u(x,t)·u_t(x,t)=0 and u_t(x,t)·(u_tt(x,t)−Δu(x,t))=0. Moreover u·u_tt=−|u_t|² and u·u_jj(j,x,t)=−|u_j(j,x,t)|² for every j∈{1,…,n}. Every scalar a satisfying u_tt−Δu=a u at (x,t) necessarily equals ∑_{j=1}^n|u_j(j,x,t)|²−|u_t(x,t)|²; thus the explicit sphere wave-map equation is a consequence, not an extra assumption.

locals.declaration: Fix an arbitrary spatial point x.
Choose a scalar a given by H005 at (x,t), so u_tt(x,t)−Δu(x,t)=a u(x,t).
For the spatial second-derivative identity, fix any j∈{1,…,n}.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary x∈ℝ^n and t>0. H004 gives u·u=1 on the whole domain. The time section is differentiable near t by H002. Applying M006 with both functions equal to this section gives 0=∂_t(u·u)=2u·u_t, hence u·u_t=0. Whenever a source is formulated for a function on all of ℝ, a time section may be set to zero for nonpositive times; it agrees with the given section on a neighborhood of t, so its derivative at t is unchanged. This convention is only for applying sources and does not define u at time zero.

produces.statement: For every spatial point y∈ℝ^n and every positive time r, u(y,r)·u_t(y,r)=0.

argument.text: Choose a from H005 at (x,t). Dot its identity with u_t. F001 at (x,t) and symmetry of the Euclidean dot product give u_t·(u_tt−Δu)=a(u_t·u)=0. Only this pointwise choice is used; a is never differentiated.

Retain also the supplied explicit equation calculation. Since F001 is an identity on an open time interval, M006 applied to the time sections of u and u_t gives 0=∂_t(u·u_t)=|u_t|²+u·u_tt, so u·u_tt=−|u_t|². For any fixed j, apply M006 first to u with itself along a spatial coordinate line, obtaining u·u_j=0 from H004, and then to u and u_j along that line, obtaining u·u_jj=−|u_j|². All sections and their derivatives are differentiable by H002. Dot the equation defining a with u. Since u·u=1, a=u·u_tt−∑_j u·u_jj=∑_j|u_j|²−|u_t|². The last computation works for every scalar satisfying the normality equation, and does not give it any assumed regularity. Together with F001 and F002, universal introduction in x,t and the arbitrary spatial index proves all the asserted tangency and normal-acceleration identities.
